neutral_facts.value: The prosecution case is that six persons, heavily armed with two of them carrying firearms, killed the victim in broad daylight between 12 and 12:30 p.m. The victim was present at the scene and was surrounded by the accused. The accused, including two individuals with firearms, fired multiple shots, resulting in multiple firearm entry wounds as confirmed by medical evidence. The victim died as a result of these injuries. The accused threatened the villagers present at the scene and then fled. The medical report corroborates the prosecution's account of the injuries caused by firearms and sharp-edged weapons. The trial court acquitted the accused, but the High Court overturned this decision, finding the medical evidence supported the eyewitness accounts. The Supreme Court upheld the High Court's decision, concluding that the eyewitnesses' statements were credible and corroborated by the medical evidence.

prosecution_argument.value: The prosecution argued that six persons, including two with guns, killed the victim in broad daylight. The statements of the eye-witnesses (PW-1 and PW-2) were corroborated by PW-4 and medical evidence, supporting the prosecution's version of events.

quotes.text: The statements of these witnesses (PW-1 and PW-2) were almost identical and there were no major contradictions between them – According to PW-1, he was present at the place of incidence and immediately after occurrence dictated the complaint to PW-4

defence_argument.value: The defence argued that the statements of the eye-witnesses (PW-1 and PW-2) should not be relied upon due to their close relationship with the deceased and enmity between the parties. They also questioned the credibility of the FIR and the medical evidence.

quotes.text: It has been urged that the statements of the two witnesses PWs 1 and 2 should not be relied upon since they are closely related to the deceased and there was enmity between both the sides

legal_principle_applied.value: The Supreme Court applied the principle that the presence of eye-witnesses and their statements, when corroborated by other evidence, can be relied upon to establish the facts of the case.

sentencing_rationale.value: The final sentence was imposed because the Court found the prosecution's version of the events, supported by the eye-witnesses and medical evidence, credible and that the accused were guilty of the offences punishable under Sections 147, 148, 302/149 of the IPC.
